subtype: Approach: contingency planning for a poor attempt [Thinking]
passage: Farhan, you say your whole life rides on clearing it this year. Sit, let me, Yusuf, tell you what I did. Three months before my exam, one night I stopped studying and made two columns: "If it goes well" and "If it goes badly". The second column was scary. So I filled it slowly. Second exam in October, so one more chance. A master's entrance in the spring. A job at a friend's uncle's firm if I needed rent money. Then I looked at it and thought: none of these ends my life. It felt like a net under a trapeze. I studied better after that, not worse. On exam morning my mother said, "Whatever happens, come home and eat." I came home and ate. It was a bad day, and I was fine.

qa.q: How many columns did Yusuf make on that night?
What was Yusuf feeling when filling in the second column?
qa.a: Yusuf felt scared at first, then calmer as the backup routes appeared, likening the list to a net under a trapeze.

qa.q: What choice inside the story helped Yusuf study better, and why?
qa.a: Yusuf wrote out backup routes for a bad result, because the fear of one bad day being the end of everything shrank once other paths were on paper.

qa.q: How might Yusuf's mother have seen the exam morning?
qa.a: Yusuf's mother wanted Yusuf home and fed whatever happened, so the mother seems to have put wellbeing above the result.

grounding: Shows contingency planning: quietly mapping alternative routes so that one poor attempt does not feel like the end.

subtype: Approach: contingency planning for a poor attempt [Thinking]
passage: Three weeks before the engineering services exam, Irfan's grandfather fell ill, and Irfan spent most days at the hospital in Aligarh instead of at his desk. One evening on the hospital bench, he let the question in: what if the exam goes badly? Instead of pushing it away, he opened a note on his phone. "If it goes wrong: 1. The state engineering exam in August, mostly the same syllabus. 2. The postgraduate entrance in February. 3. Apply to the two firms that came to campus; they hire through the year." His friend Lakshmi, preparing for the same exam, called that night. "You sound calmer," she said. "I made a Plan B, C and D," he told her. "It's strange. Knowing one bad day isn't the end makes me less scared of the day." He revised for an hour on the bench before visiting hours ended.

qa.q: When is the state engineering exam?
How did Irfan feel after making the backup list?
qa.a: Irfan felt calmer and less scared, knowing one bad day wouldn't be the end.

qa.q: What else could Irfan do with the backup plan?
qa.a: Irfan could note the dates and forms for each route, so switching quickly is easy if needed.

qa.q: How does Lakshmi notice the change?
qa.a: Lakshmi hears it in his voice on the call and says he sounds calmer.

grounding: Shows a candidate quietly working out backup routes, such as a second exam, a postgraduate entrance or a job, so one bad day is not the end.

subtype: Approach: contingency planning for a poor attempt [Thinking]
passage: On the local train home to Borivali, Nilesh did something he had avoided for months. He opened a blank page in his notebook and wrote at the top: "If prelims doesn't happen this year." His heart thumped just writing it. Then he made himself continue. Option one: the state civil services exam in October, with a lot of overlap. Option two: the MA entrance in spring, since he liked political science anyway. Option three: a job at the policy research firm where his friend Hansa worked, which had asked for his resume twice. By Dadar the page was full. He noticed his shoulders had come down. The prelims was still the plan. But it was no longer the only door, and somehow that made studying for it feel lighter. That night, when Hansa texted "how's prep?", he replied, "Good. I have exits now."

qa.q: What did Nilesh write at the top of the page?
qa.a: If prelims doesn't happen this year.

qa.q: How did Nilesh feel while writing the heading?
qa.a: Nilesh felt anxious, his heart thumping just writing it.

qa.q: What else could Nilesh do to keep the backups ready?
qa.a: Nilesh could note the deadlines for each option and send the resume to Hansa's firm, so the options stay real.

qa.q: How might Hansa see Nilesh's reply?
qa.a: Hansa may be pleased and relieved to hear him sound settled, and glad the firm is one of his exits.

grounding: Illustrates a candidate writing down backup routes such as another exam, a postgraduate entrance or a job, so one poor attempt would not end everything.
